title: Karl Bushby Walks Home After 28 Years
summary:
It took Karl Bushby 28 years to walk home.

Bushby, a British adventurer, is the first person to travel around the world on foot or by swimming. He set off from Punta Arenas in Chile on 1 November 1998, aged 29. He thought the trip of about 31,000 miles would take 12 years. On 2 November 2026, he reached his mother's home in Hull, England.

It began with a birthday card from his father, about walking from London to New York through the Bering Strait. He would move only by walking or swimming, and would not go home until he finished.

He started with a basic survival kit, a cart and about 500 dollars, and no sponsors. Strangers often shared food and shelter.

In 2006, he and Dimitri Kieffer crossed the icy Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia, walking about 150 miles in temperatures as low as minus 31 degrees Fahrenheit.

He swam the Channel for about 20 hours over three days, reaching Dover on 5 October, then walked about 250 more miles to Hull, where his mother Angela was waiting.
why_it_matters: Bushby's journey shows that sticking with a hard goal, one small step at a time, can help you finish something that seems impossible.

background_read: Karl Bushby is an adventurer who set out to travel all the way around the world using only walking and swimming.
His rule was simple: he would not go home until he had finished the whole journey, so he had to cross land and sea on foot.
Along the way strangers often shared food and shelter, which helped him keep going through cold and lonely places.
Article_Structure: WHO: Karl Bushby, a British adventurer, with Dimitri Kieffer on part of the journey and his mother Angela waiting at the end.
WHAT: He travelled around the world on foot or by swimming and finally reached his mother's home in Hull.
WHERE: From Punta Arenas in Chile, through the Bering Strait and across the Channel to Dover, then on to Hull in England.
WHY: He wanted to finish the journey his father's birthday card had suggested, moving only by walking or swimming and not going home until it was done.
